title: Rare k-mers reveal centromere haplogroups underlying human diversity and cancer translocations
title_zh: 稀有k-元揭示人类多样性与癌症易位背后的着丝粒单倍群
abstract: Human centromeres are highly variable but remain among the least characterized regions of the genome because their repetitive structure has hindered conventional analysis of population diversity and disease relevance. Here, we show that rare k-mers in centromeric regions capture lineage-specific variation, defining discrete haplogroups with distinct structural features. We developed ascairn to infer these haplogroups from short-read whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data. Applying this framework to >3,300 genomes reveals extensive global diversity in centromere haplogroups and signatures of population history. Analyzing short-read WGS data from 142 oligodendroglioma cases with 1p/19q co-deletion, we mapped breakpoints to the centromere regions of chromosomes 1 and 19, revealing a clear positional relationship to kinetochore attachment sites and a link between centromere haplotype structure and rearrangement susceptibility. Rare k-mers thus open centromeres to population-scale analysis, linking centromere structural diversity to human evolutionary history and disease-associated genomic instability.
abstract_zh: 人类着丝粒高度可变，但仍是基因组中研究最少的区域之一，因为其重复结构阻碍了传统的人群多样性和疾病相关性分析。在本研究中，我们展示了着丝粒区域中稀有k-元能够捕捉谱系特异性变异，定义具有不同结构特征的离散单倍群。我们开发了ascairn工具，利用短读段全基因组测序（WGS）数据推断这些单倍群。将该框架应用于超过3,300个基因组，揭示了着丝粒单倍群的广泛全球多样性以及人群历史的迹象。对142例具有1p/19q共缺失的少突胶质瘤病例的短读段WGS数据进行分析，我们将断点映射到染色体1和19的着丝粒区域，显示出与纺锤体附着位点的明显位置关系，并揭示了着丝粒单倍型结构与重排易感性之间的联系。稀有k-元因此为大规模人群分析打开了着丝粒的研究窗口，将着丝粒结构多样性与人类进化史及疾病相关基因组不稳定性相连接。
